interpretation: Shared-host CPU interference is directly observed during the 1321ms carrier32 measurement: other Java processes reach ~180-210 cores, runnable queue reaches 546. This experiment cannot establish that carrier32 itself causes degradation.

The same bad latest run has 1788.834s cumulative Cursor monitor wait, 58544 recorded waits, max 664.138ms. 74912 requests >=20ms, only 4842 overlap GC. Contention and backlog coincide with routing delay; GC alone cannot explain it.
Default latest run A has ForkJoinPool.scan at 74.409% (3k) / 72.905% (10k) Java execution samples; latest run B is near zero. This is separate from idle parks/native epoll samples.

Planner32 controls reduce recorded Cursor wait to 0.486 / 0.365s at 10k from 9.223 / 14.295s in default runs, but host load differs, so effect size is not a clean causal estimate. Latest planner32 client P99 is 40.806 / 53.348ms; not stable user SLO.
Latest carrier32-a fails 10k warmup with terminal record retains request-owned state and one retained request. There is no 10k formal measurement in that fork.

Next code focus: shorten shared address rotation critical section while preserving fair address-ring and dynamic eligibility; validate planner concurrency under monitored isolated load; reduce full-fleet snapshot/projection allocation. Do not adopt carrier32 alone or declare regression fixed.
measurement_limits: All results here include JFR diagnostic overhead; not unprofiled acceptance evidence.
Host CPU isolation was not available; overlapping host workloads confound parameter comparisons.
Cursor wait is accumulated across threads; conditional wait P99 is not request P99. Slow-request population is >=20ms only.
Allocation weights are statistical sample estimates, include protobuf parsing on Master and Mock, and are not exact allocations.
No new production source changes, UT gate, or 50ms threshold relaxation in this diagnostic turn.
